```plato
    //==
    // # IProcedural motion evaluation
    //
    // The `ITimeVarying<Number>` obligation of `Oscillator`
    // (`motion-graphics.types.plato`): the signal
    // `Bias + Amplitude * wave(Frequency * time + Phase)` the type's doc comment
    // states, one waveform per case.
    //
    // Every waveform is normalized to [-1, 1] and phase-aligned with the sine, so
    // switching waveform changes the shape and nothing else — the signal still
    // leaves zero rising at phase zero and peaks a quarter turn later. That
    // alignment is why the triangle is written around a quarter-turn shift rather
    // than as the more obvious `2|2t - 1| - 1`.

    // The unit-amplitude waveform value at a phase angle, in [-1, 1].
    WaveformValue(waveform: OscillatorWaveform, phase: Angle): Number {
        var turns = phase.Turns;
        var cycle = turns - turns.Floor;
        var shifted = turns + 0.25 - (turns + 0.25).Floor;
        return match (waveform) {
            Sine => phase.Sin;
            // The sign of the sine: a hard edge at every zero crossing.
            Square => phase.Sin >= 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0;
            Triangle => 1.0 - 4.0 * (shifted - 0.5).Abs;
            // A rising ramp: -1 at the start of the cycle, +1 at its end.
            Sawtooth => 2.0 * cycle - 1.0;
            // Smooth pseudo-random: one dimension of lattice value noise walked
            // along the phase, so successive cycles differ but the signal stays
            // continuous.
            Noise => ValueNoise2D(0, 1.0).Eval(Point2D(turns, 0.0));
        };
    }
```
